{{Short description|Czech mathematician (1933–2018)}}
[[File:Zdenek Hedrlin.png|thumb|Image of Zdenek Hedrlin]]
'''Zdeněk Hedrlín''' (1933 – April 22, 2018) was a Czech mathematician, specializing in [[universal algebra]] and combinatorial theory, both in pure and applied mathematics.

Zdeněk Hedrlín received his PhD from Prague's [[Charles University]] in 1963. His thesis on commutative semigroups was supervised by [[Miroslav Katětov]].<ref name=MathGen>{{MathGenealogy|id=59157}}</ref> Hedrlín held the title of [[Academic ranks in the Czech Republic and in Slovakia|''Docent'' (associated professor)]] at Charles University, working at the Faculty of Mathematics and Physics for over 60 years until he died at age 85. He was among the first Czech mathematicians to do research on [[category theory]].<ref name=obit>{{cite web|author=Kratochvíl, Jan|title=Zemřel doc. Zdeněk Hedrlín (deceased docent Zdeněk Hedrlín)|website=Matematicko-fyzikální fakulty Univerzity Karlovy (Mathematics and Physics Faculty of Charles University)|date=April 26, 2018|url=https://www.mff.cuni.cz/cs/verejnost/aktuality/zemrel-doc-zdenek-hedrlin}}</ref> 

{{blockquote|Already in the mid-1960s, the Prague school of Zdeněk Hedrlín, Aleš Pultr and [[Věra Trnková]] had devised a particularly nice notion of concrete categories over [[Functor category|'''''Set''''', the so-called ''functor-structured categories'']] ...<ref name="KoslowskiMelton2012">{{cite book|editor1=Koslowski, Jürgen|editor2=Melton, Austin|chapter=Chapter. ''Contributions and importance of Professor George E. Strecker's Research'' by Jürgen Koslowski|title=Categorical Perspectives|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PjzTBwAAQBAJ&pg=PA73|date=6 December 2012|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-1-4612-1370-3|pages=63–90}} (quote from p. 73)</ref>}}

In 1970 Hedrlín was an Invited Speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Nice]].<ref>{{cite book|author=Hedrlín, Z.|year=1970|chapter=Extensions of structures and full embeddings of categories|title=''In:'' Actes du Congrès international des mathématiciens, 1–10 Septembre 1970, Nice|volume=1|pages=319–321}}</ref> In the later part of his career, he focused on applications of relational structures and led very successful special and interdisciplinary seminars. Applications to biological cell behavior earned him and his students a European grant.<ref name=obit/> (He and his students worked on computational cell models of cancer.)

Hedrlín was a member of the editorial board of the ''[[Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Managing Editors; Editors|website=Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra|url=https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/82484794.pdf}}</ref> His [[Erdős number]] is 1.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1016/0012-365X(72)90087-8|title=Ramsey's theorem and self-complementary graphs|year=1972|last1=Chvatal|first1=V.|last2=Erdös|first2=P.|last3=Hedrlín|first3=Z.|journal=Discrete Mathematics|volume=3|issue=4|pages=301–304|doi-access=free}}</ref> His doctoral students include [[Vojtěch Rödl]] and [[Svatopluk Poljak]].<ref name=MathGen/>
